mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen every week for the last four weeks (-35.7 to -28.6), indicating a gradual commuter return. This ongoing improvement in workplace attendance mechanically raises weekday retail and recreation footfall, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise each week, or if RETAIL_REC falls while WORKPLACES improves, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week TRANSIT improvement exceeding 3 percentage points for two consecutive weeks signals accelerated return of commuting and leisure travel, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks as transit-dependent visitors resume city-centre trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT rose from -29.6 at t-2w to -23.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses this threshold but RETAIL_REC does not rise, or instead falls, within the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a compounding return-to-routine effect: commuters both travel more and work more in person, jointly amplifying retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, producing a positive RETAIL_REC trend over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two weeks but the resulting RETAIL_REC rise over the next four weeks is no larger than the rise observed when only one series improves, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for four consecutive weeks (7.6 to 4.7), indicating households are spending less time at home. In a post-restriction normalization regime this behavioral shift away from home-centric activity directly substitutes into more retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.6 at t-3w to 4.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues declining but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks, or the regime shifts to renewed stay-at-home behavior, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has weakened sharply from +12.3 to +4.6 over the last four weeks, consistent with early-autumn seasonal decline in outdoor activity. As outdoor recreation options shrink, demand substitutes toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS fell from 12.3 at t-2w to 4.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to decline through the autumn period but RETAIL_REC does not rise, or actually falls, over the next 28 days, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES exceeding 5 points signals accelerated employer return-to-office mandates. This policy-driven surge in office attendance quickly lifts nearby retail and recreation footfall within one week of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES rose 9.2 points between t-2w (-38.4) and t-1w (-29.4)
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES jumps more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not rise within the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has steadily improved (-9.4 to -5.1) while RESIDENTIAL has declined (7.6 to 4.7); jointly these indicate a behavioral shift from home-bound essential-only shopping toward broader out-of-home consumption, which together predict a stronger rise in RETAIL_REC than either series alone over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently but the RETAIL_REC rise over the next two weeks is no greater than what either series would predict alone, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In the autumn back-to-school/work regime, any TRANSIT week-on-week gain signals immediate resumption of weekday commuting patterns that quickly translate into higher retail footfall near transit hubs within one week.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves week-on-week during this regime but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the hypothesis is rejected.
